messages:
Priya: Starting bring-up for MeridianLite-13B (community compat). Quick smoke: generation matches baseline on short prompts but embeddings drop ~0.028 on semantic-lite. Also saw weird token split on sequences with U+200D (ZWJ).

Ken: Any tokenizer diffs? unicode normalizer differences often cause those splits. Which exporter used?

Priya: Used modelkit v1.2 default convert. Tokenizer diff: common tokens 50000 -> 49985 (-15), unmapped fallbacks 22 (mostly ZWJ, variation selectors). Example: '👩‍💻' tokenized as two tokens on our side but single on model side.

Arjun: That collapsing explains embedding drift for phrases heavy in emoji. Also check rotary params: model header lists freq_base=10000.0 and scale=1.000 but no per-head flags. If token ids moved, KV cache + rotary angle indexing can lead to phase aliasing when using cached sessions.

Priya: Re-ran with explicit tokenmap export: `convert --explicit-tokenmap --preserve-zwj`. Early coords: embeddings delta reduced to ~0.012 on 10-sample probe. Will kick a full semantic-lite run.

build-bot: ci:semantic-lite-run queued (job: 1795555600) for meridianlite/onboard. Watch ML-4600 for failures.

Ken: Good. Also please run a quick quant-mode comparison: per-tensor int4 (fast) vs per-channel int4 (slower) vs int8 per-channel. If per-channel int4 with EMA calibration reduces delta, that's our path for Dedicated.

Arjun: One more experiment suggestion: tokenmap shim that temporarily maps the 22 fallback tokens to a contiguous unused block (e.g., +600k) and run a longctx continuation test. If repetition/reordering goes away, we know it's id collision rather than numeric quantization.

Priya: Will do both. Kicking per-channel int4 sweep and the shim longctx probe. If shim helps, we can publish a converter patch to preserve these emoji sequences by default.

Ken: Also add an LLR perplexity check on held-dev after remap+quant. If LLR delta > 1.0% hold.

Priya: Adding checks: embedding-diff, LLR-delta, repetition-probe. Will post full results when jobs complete. Tagging @eng-ml for visibility. :mag:
